name: Branching sessions
summary: The session is stored as a tree rather than a flat list: every entry points to its parent, and the current position is a leaf. Returning to an earlier point and continuing creates a new branch without erasing the old one, and only the active branch is sent to the model. pi, the minimal coding agent at pi.dev, implements this in its session files.
how: Give every session entry an id and a parentId
Track the current leaf; new entries become its children
To branch, move the leaf to an earlier entry and continue from there
Build model context by walking from the leaf back to the root
Optionally summarise the abandoned branch and attach it to the new one
facts: JSONL entries linked by id/parentId (session format v2+)
Only the active branch reaches the model
pi adds summary entries and does not delete originals
Exploration without losing work, but harder to read and sync than a linear log
watchOut: File edits on disk are not rewound by switching branches unless paired with checkpoints
Trees are harder to export and display than linear transcripts
